newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman shares up on plans to scrap foreign ceilings.
newsitem.headline: Amman shares up on plans to scrap foreign ceilings.

text.p: The announcement of plans to scrap foreign ownership ceilings on most listed companies gave the Amman stock exchange index a modest boost on Tuesday.

But a majority of shares fell and brokers said the impact of the announcement would be muted until it won cabinet approval, and would be limited to stocks whose levels of foreign ownership had already reached the existing limit of 50 percent.
Three economic sectors - construction, general retail trade and mining - were excluded from the new ruling.
Arab Bank and Jordan Islamic Bank, both of which have 50 percent foreign ownership, rose in busy trade.

Arab Bank rose three dinars to 255 dinars and Jordan Islamic Bank gained 0.06 dinars to 3.65 dinars, pushing the official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index up 0.56 percent to 159.54 points in turnover of 1.4 million dinars ($2 million).
But falling shares outnumbered gainers by 15 to 12, with another 10 trading and closing unchanged.

"The (foreign ownership) decision is already affecting those two banks. If Arab Bank continues to rise it should motivate the rest of the market," said Mohammad Abdallah, senior analyst at Pearl Consulting.
Arab Bank's shares account for about one third of the market's total capitalisation of 3.2 billion dinars and a number of other firms listed on the bourse hold shares in the bank.
Brokers said foreign demand continued on Jordan Cement Factory and Jordan Phosphate Mines, as well as Jordan National Bank, which rose 0.03 dinars.
Foreign ownership in Jordan National Bank is still less than 50 percent but it is a leading target among the handful of blue-chip shares sought recently by international investors.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose a modest 0.09 percent to 80.79 points, 3.12 percent down from the start of the year.
